rationale: C20 plausibly supplied a concrete drafting template. Both orders establish an interagency committee, specify its leadership and agency membership, direct it to coordinate or guide agency programs, require affected agencies to advance the program's objectives, and conclude with an almost verbatim assistance-and-detailing provision under section 214 of the May 3, 1945 act. C06 and C04 share similar council machinery and assistance clauses, but C20 provides the closest overall sequence and language.

shared_material.child_excerpt: Each department and agency responsible for functions and activities that can contribute to the objectives of the rural-development program and related activities shall carry those functions and activities forward in such a manner as to make the fullest possible contribution
shared_material.parent_excerpt: The heads of all Federal departments and agencies engaged in procurement, stockpiling, commodity price support, rate regulation, subsidy and similar programs which directly affect prices and costs shall reexamine their programs... and shall take such administrative actions or recommend such changes in legislation as are deemed desirable
shared_material.explanation: Both place an affirmative implementation duty on the departments operating programs relevant to the committee's policy objective.

shared_material.child_excerpt: The departments and agencies represented on the Committee shall, as may be necessary for the purpose of effectuating the provisions of this order, furnish assistance to the Committee in consonance with section 214 of the act of May 3, 1945, 59 Stat. 134 (31 U.S.C. 691). Such assistance may include the detailing of employees to the Committee, one of whom may serve as its executive secretary, to perform such functions consistent with the purpose of this order as the Committee may assign to them.
shared_material.parent_excerpt: The agencies designated in section 1 of this order shall, as may be necessary for the purpose of effectuating the provisions of this order, furnish assistance to the Committee in accordance with section 214 of the act of May 3, 1945 (59 Stat. 134; 31 U.S.C. 691). Such assistance may include detailing employees to the Committee, one of whom may serve as its executive officer, to perform such functions consistent with the purpose of this order as the Committee may assign to them.
shared_material.explanation: This is a nearly verbatim operative clause, with only minor substitutions such as "represented" for "designated," "consonance with" for "accordance with," and "executive secretary" for "executive officer."
